title: Frontier-lab chip-supply warrant deals enter S-1 disclosure standard by Q1 2027
body: By Q1 2027 the May 6-7 Cerebras Systems IPO above-range pricing print — $128 per share (vs $115-$125 disclosed range, +2.4% above the upper end), $3.58B raise lifted to ~$4.12B with the green-shoe exercised in full at a fully-diluted ~$27.2B market cap, OpenAI's December 2025 $1B warrant package (~33M shares, ~12% of float, struck at the Series H reference) marked publicly in-the-money on listing day, Sam Altman + Greg Brockman + Ilya Sutskever + Adam D'Angelo angel positions all crystallized at a $26.6B-target → $27.2B-actual print — combined with the May 7 SambaNova + Groq accelerated S-1 confidential-submission timelines (60-90 days), the Tenstorrent Hyundai + Samsung Foundry IPO bridge round at >$3B, and a public-market multiple now sitting under disclosed AI-accelerator revenue, force the next wave of S-1 filings (and existing AI-accelerator + frontier-lab 10-Q footnote schedules) to disclose frontier-lab chip-supply warrant and loan terms as a standard issuer-level itemized exhibit rather than buried among related-party narrative footnotes. The forcing function is that OpenAI's Cerebras warrant is the first publicly-priced data point linking a frontier lab's structured-equity supply contract to an open-market multiple; sell-side and SEC Corp Fin staff comment letters now have a quantitative comparable to press for, which converts what was bespoke disclosure into template language. The most likely shape is an itemized warrant-and-loan exhibit naming counterparty (frontier lab), strike reference (Series-letter peg), share count, coverage clause, and any minimum-revenue or capacity-take obligations; SambaNova's S-1 ships first given its ~$5.1B last-priced round and Aramco Digital + Meta API customer roster, Groq second on its Saudi-anchored vehicle and inference-tier API revenue, Tenstorrent third via its bridge-round disclosure. Bear case is that the SEC permits silence on coverage clauses pending a separate concept release; absent that, Q1 2027 lands the standardised exhibit shape across the cohort.

reasoning.because: Cerebras IPO pricing puts OpenAI's $1B warrant package publicly in-the-money on listing day May 7.
reasoning.given: SambaNova + Groq + Tenstorrent S-1 prep gives frontier-lab supply contracts a public comparable.
reasoning.so_that: S-1 and 10-Q filings disclose frontier-lab chip-supply warrant and loan terms as standard itemized exhibits.
reasoning.landing: By Q1 2027; SambaNova S-1 first, Groq second, Tenstorrent third on bridge round.
reasoning.plain_language: Cerebras went public and OpenAI's warrant deal showed up on its books, so future chip-startup IPOs will spell out their frontier-lab contract terms.

summary: Cerebras's May 7 above-range IPO marks OpenAI's $1B warrant publicly in-the-money and gives sell-side a direct comparable for frontier-lab supply contracts. By Q1 2027 SambaNova, Groq, and Tenstorrent S-1s disclose chip-supply warrant and loan terms as a standard itemized exhibit.
